svg.title: Canadian mortgage tax escrow versus paying the municipality yourself
svg.desc: A labelled $6,000 annual property tax is $500 a month in escrow plus a cushion. After a 10 percent reassessment the monthly tax portion can jump by about $50, and a shortage catch-up can add several hundred dollars in one statement. Self-pay needs the same $500 parked before the instalment date.
svg.text: Escrow is a calendar, not a fixed mortgage payment
Labelled $6,000 annual tax. Ontario 2026 assessments still use 1 Jan 2016 CVA (MPAC). B.C. 2026 roll is 1 Jul 2025 value.
A 10% value or rate jump on $6,000 is $600/year ($50/month). If the account is short mid-year, the lender can spread a catch-up - here a labelled $400 - across remaining payments.
Self-pay: four $1,500 city instalments still need $500/month parked. Missing a due date is penalties, not a mortgage conversation.
First-year owners: the statement of adjustments is not the annual bill. Confirm with the lender and the municipality. Not brokerage advice.
